name: InterContinental New York Barclay
positioning: Historic 1926 Midtown Manhattan hotel near Grand Central Station, with rooms inspired by Park Avenue's residential style
best_for: Travelers who want a historic Midtown base near Grand Central and Rockefeller Center
Guests drawn to literary and New York history

facts.text: The Barclay first opened its doors in 1926.
The hotel was originally part of Grand Central Terminal's urban design plan.
The hotel has a grand staircase, Federalist-inspired details and an intricate lobby ceiling.
Ernest Hemingway completed the final revisions of For Whom the Bell Tolls at the hotel.
In 1945 The Barclay introduced the first-ever hotel lobby birdcage, filled with songbirds.
In 1996 Bill Clinton used The Barclay as his New York campaign headquarters.
The hotel is near Grand Central Station.
The hotel is near Rockefeller Center.
Rooms and suites have stylish decor, marble bathrooms, eclectic artwork and expansive city views.
Guest rooms and suites are inspired by Park Avenue's residential style.
The Parlour restaurant pays tribute to the hotel's 1920s origin.
The fitness center is open 24 hours and includes a Peloton bike.

highlights.text: The Barclay was designed in neo-Federal, American Colonial style by Cross and Cross, the firm behind the Tiffany & Co. building.
Rooftop gardens and beehives supply fresh herbs and house-harvested honey for dishes and cocktails at The Parlour.
Top of the Rock is a quick three-block walk away, and the concierge can organize a VIP tour that skips the lines.
Suites have marble bathrooms with heated floors and custom toiletries.
The B Suite Collection by Barclay offers individually appointed suites.

considerations.text: The hotel does not have a pool.
WhataHotel notes a busy Midtown location with heavy pedestrian traffic.
